title: Hackmd-Api-Url header lets any HTTP caller point the server (and its env token) at any URL
reason: In TRANSPORT=http mode an unauthenticated request can send only the Hackmd-Api-Url header (or ?config=base64 JSON) with an attacker URL; the server then falls back to the operator's HACKMD_API_TOKEN and sends it as a bearer token to that URL on every tool call (token theft), and can also be aimed at internal hosts or 169.254.169.254 (SSRF). ConfigSchema only checks it is a string.
fix: Do not accept the API URL from requests (env/config only), or allowlist https://api.hackmd.io; never combine a request-supplied URL with the server's env token; block private/link-local addresses.

title: HTTP /mcp endpoint has no authentication and falls back to the operator's token
reason: Any client that reaches the port (listen binds all interfaces) gets read/write/delete access to the HackMD account whose token is in the env, without presenting any credential — a confused deputy with one static upstream credential.
fix: In HTTP mode require each caller to send its own token (no env fallback), or add real authentication on /mcp; bind to 127.0.0.1 unless deployed behind an authenticating proxy.

title: CORS defaults to '*' and allows the token/URL headers
reason: With no CORS_ORIGIN set, any web page the user visits can send cross-origin POSTs to a local/remote HTTP instance and drive all tools with the env token (and set Hackmd-Api-Url for M001); no Origin/Host check guards against DNS rebinding.
fix: Default to no CORS (or an explicit allowlist) and validate Origin/Host headers on /mcp.

title: Untrusted note content + private notes + a way to publish them, no approval
reason: get_note / list_team_notes return note bodies (often written by teammates or guests) raw into the model; injected text there can make the agent read private notes and then create_note/update_note with readPermission 'guest' to publish them, or delete notes.
fix: Mark note content as untrusted data in results, require user confirmation for permission changes, deletes and creates, and consider dropping readPermission/writePermission from the tool schema.

title: delete_note / delete_team_note / update tools act immediately
reason: Destructive tools have destructiveHint annotations but no server-side confirmation or dry-run; whether a human approves depends on the MCP client's settings.
fix: Keep the annotations and make sure clients do not auto-approve these tools; optionally add a confirm parameter / soft-delete.
